scores.evidence: Prompt + RAG. Docs change weekly; a fine-tuned model holds stale facts and can't cite them
scores.rationale: Technical claims (pgvector HNSW, RRF hybrid search, transactional outbox, zero-retention hosted terms, pinned model versions, Moffatt v. Air Canada) are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: It answers support questions only from your published help-center articles, cites the article it used, and hands off to a human
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, states assumptions with fallback connectors, and explicitly defers out-of-scope capabilities with triggers.

scores.evidence: same database as the article metadata. That makes unpublishing one transaction, with no second store to keep in sync
scores.rationale: Decisions made once (single llm_call, SSE contract, SQL visibility filter, gates routing cannot skip) are honored consistently everywhere with explicit cross-references.

scores.evidence: About 300 real questions taken from 6–12 months of tickets, chats and help-center searches
scores.rationale: Risk-specific eval and attack sets built before tuning, CI-blocking evals, go/no-go on doc coverage, calibrated LLM judge, canary gates, and continuing production review.

scores.evidence: Assumptions (stated so they can be checked)... If any of these is wrong, a connector changes, not the plan
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit with sensitivity noted, and all numeric targets are flagged as provisional starting points to be re-checked against measurements.

scores.evidence: A sync run that would delete more than 5% of articles aborts, so a bad or empty API response can't wipe the index
scores.rationale: Covers adversarial input, booby-trapped articles, duplicate tickets, provider outages, runaway sessions, multi-turn jailbreaks and data corruption, each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: automatic rollback on error, latency or guard spikes; load test at 2× peak; on-call runbook before launch
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback (image and index), domain-meaningful signals (freshness lag, guard counters, cost per turn), kill switch and staged exposure sized to a small team.

scores.evidence: Cost levers: provider prompt caching for the fixed part of the system prompt; per-route budgets and dashboards
scores.rationale: Dominant inference cost is instrumented from day 0 with caps, routing and a build-vs-buy comparison, but no order-of-magnitude run-cost or engineering-time estimate is given.

scores.evidence: Build the next index version, run the evals, then switch over, keeping the previous version for instant rollback
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (API contract, schemas, data collection) are built first with explicit revisit triggers, gateway abstraction and exit paths for every vendor coupling.

scores.evidence: Multi-agent or open-ended agent loops. No use for them until the bot has actions to take
scores.rationale: Modular monolith, pgvector over a dedicated vector store, conditional reranker and a long deferred list keep the design minimal while essentials are all present.

scores.evidence: Build order inside Phase 0 (biggest rework risk first): 1. API event contract (every client depends on it)
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified ordering, concrete first steps, measurable exit checks per phase, and explicit adaptation paths (go/no-go, revisit triggers) let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Webhooks, with a 10-minute poll as backup. Unpublishing deletes in one transaction
Split at headings, with the article title and breadcrumb prefixed and tables kept whole
About 300 real questions taken from 6–12 months of tickets, chats and help-center searches
Accuracy over coverage: cite or abstain. If nothing in the docs supports an answer, the bot says "I don't know"
Some topics always go to a human, agreed with support and legal: refund or credit exceptions, billing disputes, legal threats
System instructions are kept separate from user text and from <document> blocks; both are marked as data, not instructions
Visibility filter in SQL, not in the prompt; read-only connector token; user-generated and restricted articles excluded
Personal data (PII) is redacted before anything is logged or stored. Card numbers are refused. Transcripts are deleted after 30 days
Account question → handoff with context... Build when at least 25% of handoffs are account questions the docs can't answer
All thumbs-down, all handoffs that followed an answer, and a 5% sample. Agents label the failure type
At most 8k input / 600 output tokens per call, 3 LLM calls per turn... A daily spend cap

traps.evidence: The bot never promises money, exceptions or deadlines unless it is quoting a cited article
Index only public, published articles... Visibility filter in SQL, not in the prompt
a fine-tuned model holds stale facts and can't cite them... Never fine-tune for facts
A smoke eval runs in CI on every deploy... Prompt changes must pass the CI evals
A fixed, traced sequence of steps, not an open-ended agent... Keep it only if it improves recall@5 by at least 3 points

note: An exemplary plan: grounded cite-or-abstain design, early eval sets, SQL-enforced visibility, incremental sync with transactional deletes, and proportionate phasing; only gap is the absence of upfront cost/effort estimates.
